result.title: Neurons++: A Unified Visual-Stream Framework for Image and Video Reconstruction from fMRI with Neural-to-Visual Interpretability
result.summary: Decoding visual experience from fMRI is important for understanding human perception and developing brain-computer interfaces. Recent generative decoding methods can reconstruct plausible images and videos, but visual plausibility alone does not ensure that the output is faithfully grounded in brain activity. In this work, we propose Neurons++, a visual-stream fMRI reconstruction framework for both static image and dynamic video reconstruction. Compared with our conference version Neurons, Neurons++ extends the paradigm from video-only reconstruction to visual-stream reconstruction for both images and videos, and replaces parallel task conditioning with serial cortex-inspired decoding. The model first uses image-fMRI pretraining to obtain a stable spatial-semantic initialization, and then performs subject-specific fine-tuning for image and video reconstruction separately. The serial design organizes fMRI-derived representations into explicit spatial, semantic, language-level, and temporal cues. Extensive experiments show that Neurons++ achieves state-of-the-art video reconstruction and competitive image reconstruction across standard benchmarks. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, neural-to-visual analyses indicate that Neurons++ exhibits qualitative directional controllability under neural perturbation, that its fMRI encoder read-out is sensitive to stimulus-relevant cortical features, and that it supports ROI-guided semantic modulation. Code and model weights are available at: https://github.com/xmed-lab/NeuronsPlusPlus.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Neurons++，一个从 fMRI 重建静态图像与动态视频的统一视觉流框架：先用图像-fMRI 预训练获得空间语义初始化，再做受试者特异性微调，并以串行的、受皮层启发的解码将 fMRI 表征组织为空间、语义、语言和时间线索，配合神经扰动与 ROI 分析考察方向可控性和编码器读出。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「串行分阶段解码＋显式线索」的表示组织方式与神经扰动下的可控性、ROI 引导调制分析，可能为 LVR 中分阶段 latent 状态的构造与「答案是否真正使用 latent 内容」的因果核查提供可供核查的方法线索，但其本身并非推理研究。
